objective: Astra's, one correction objective with direction and size. Every native answer step and question position of the 30 fitting answers (19,751 rows) at all 105 merges is asked where the recipient-prefix field puts that row's state (its unit direction and the log of its size, in the relative-state metric). A correct answer's rows ask for its own recorded trajectory (9,255 rows); a wrong answer's question rows and its answer rows before the row that wrote its wrong sign ask for its own original state (4,907 rows); its rows from that row to its end ask for its matched successful counterpart, as the matched field does (5,589 rows). No row, layer or merge is cropped, weighted away or protected apart: a row that asks to stay is a request in the same sum, read again after every earlier write. The field is an experimental fitting objective and no validated capability target.

hypothesis: Marcos's, for round two: a capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, and editing the weights where that recurring difference lives repairs the capability. This run's own, as Astra states the experiment: in the matched field the request on a wrong answer's question and on its rows before the wrong sign was a request for another question's state, which pressed the model to copy a success's legitimate quantities and wording; with those rows asked for the answer's own original state and the whole request from the sign's row on kept, the copying goes and the useful correction stays. It is a counterfactual assumption about which rows' counterpart was wrong. It is no finding that the state before the sign is right, or that the gap begins at the sign.
why_this_direction: Step 5 of the method is the edit on the computation discrepancy along the whole path: one objective with direction and size, the correct group in the same objective, a full sweep in path order. The matched-context sweep (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/whole-gap-mates-original) is the first such sweep read on the model's own answers. On them no wrong answer states the gain subtracted any more (all 15 did), 7 of the 15 are whole and right and 14 of the 15 correct ones still are; and the complete sum against its field rose from 0.067494 to 0.086213, the wrong members' falling to 0.049883 and the correct members' rising from nothing to 0.036329. Its own records say where that field asked for something that is not the gap: 4 wrong answers write a kinetic energy that is not their own, exactly the 4 whose mass and speed no fitting success has; 4 answers write the gain twice at a formula whose equals sign is written again (14 such places in 8 answers where the original's thirty hold 0); and a wrong answer shares 0.65 of its lines with a success its target was made of where it shared 0.27 (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/whole-gap-mates-original/stated-numbers.json, text-pairs.json). The line of the kinetic energy and the line of the gain stand before the row that writes the sign, where the field asked every row of a wrong answer for another question's state. Performance's reading of the sign's row (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/sign-route-whole-gap-mates/result.json) found the swept weights favour the plus at 12 of 15 wrong rows on the recorded wording: at those the corrected sign does not rest on the earlier rows being rewritten. From that Astra specified one variant and this seat compiled it (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/recipient-prefix-target-original/result.json): each wrong answer keeps its own original state at its question rows and at its answer rows before the row that wrote the minus (4,907 rows) and its matched counterpart from that row to its end (5,589 rows); the correct answers keep their own trajectories (9,255 rows). What the matched field asked of the original at the kept rows was 0.138 of its whole request (0.009311 of 0.067494), so the original's control sum under the new field is 0.058182, all of it at the wrong answers' rows from the sign on. The solver, the rule, the order of the matrices, the groups left out, the card and the readers are the matched sweep's, so that what differs between the two runs' results is the field, as far as one sweep can show it (limits). What no record shows is what 70 matrices in sequence do when 14,162 of 19,751 rows ask to stay and 5,589 ask for a counterpart: that is what this run asks.
repeating_pattern_check: What has happened more than once, why, and what this run does about it. (1) The matrices' held readings fell and the complete sum on the model's own answers rose: both whole-gap sweeps, the matched one at all 70 matrices. Why, as far as the records go: a matrix's held reading is on the recordings' text and at its own merges, while the complete sum is on the text the swept model writes, where every answer's wording had changed and the correct answers' rows, asked to stay, had moved (their sum 0.036329 from nothing). This run keeps the rule, on Astra's specification, so that one thing is varied: it tests whether that rise came from the field's request before the sign. If the complete sum rises again with that request gone, the cause is not there, and what stands accused next is the rule's reading on the recordings' text and the size of what it writes, not another assignment of rows. (2) Writes of 1% of a matrix or more over several matrices broke correct answers or their text: the dose record (records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-what-made-the-edits-work/notes/compare-dose-and-geometry/notes.md; records/KNOWN.md, "dose versus breakage"), the affine sweep (writes of 0.172 of a matrix at the median, 10 of 30 answers running to the length limit) and the matched sweep (writes of 0.000 to 0.310 of a matrix, 0.057 at the median, 1% or more at 53 of 70; all 30 texts changed and 1 correct answer lost). This seat's declaration of the affine sweep did not lay that sweep beside the dose record. Laid beside it now: the rule is the same, the request is 0.862 of the matched field's at the original and 4,907 more rows ask to stay, so the writes are expected smaller than the matched sweep's and of its order, at 1% or more at many matrices; by the dose record the answers' wording is then expected to change again and the correct answers to be moved again. That is named here beforehand, its sizes are in every matrix's record, and it is read in the result. No size is capped: a cap would be a second change beside the field, Astra's specification admits none, and no record derives one. (3) A target that asks for more than the gap: both whole-gap fields asked every row of a wrong answer for a successful counterpart. The old A2, the one construction that carried to answers no fit used, asked its counterpart on the erroneous passages only (records/retrospectives/2026-11-13-parallel-constructions-astra.md). This run tests that pattern at one boundary: the rows before the wrong sign ask for the recipient's own state. (4) A request narrowed until it no longer covers the path: the constructions of November 12 to 14 asked 14 to 52 rows at a sign and edited at most six matrices, and none repaired the wrong group (STATE.md). Here nothing is cropped: all 19,751 rows and all 105 merges are in the sum, all 70 matrices are visited, and a row that asks to stay is a request, read again after every earlier write, not a row left out. (5) A text held to a request that cannot hold it: after the matched sweep every one of the 15 correct answers left its recording's text before its own sign row (first at step 6 to 99) though each of its rows asked to stay, as did every wrong answer (step 3 to 69). A request on the recordings' text does not hold a near tie of the model's own choice. So this run does not predict that the text before the sign stays the recording's token for token; it predicts that what was copied from another question goes, and reads the two apart (prediction 3). (6) A difference between two runs read as the thing varied when the runs differed in more: the two cards word 9 of 30 answers differently and a solve does not repeat bit for bit (STATE.md, the walls). Here the solves, the passes and the readers are on the matched sweep's card, the solver's files are that sweep's but for one (solver.since_the_matched_sweep), and what else differs in the execution is named (limits). No repeat of the matched sweep exists, so how far two sweeps of one declaration stand apart is not measured, and a small difference is not read as the field's. (7) This seat said more than a reading showed (the stand-in map; a cause ruled out on one look). Here the prediction is stated in what the two comparisons and the text readings measure, and the result is composed from the records by script. (8) A next step taken because the last number was bad. This run is not taken because the matched sweep's sum rose: it is one stated assumption about which rows' counterpart was wrong, drawn from what the answers wrote, specified by the objective's owner before the field existed, with what would weaken it named.
what_went_wrong_before: The first attempt at round two was deleted because it never built on the overlap. The constructions of November 12 to 14 each edited at most six matrices and none repaired the wrong group; they were stopped on November 14 (journal/2026-11-14-whole-gap-restart.md). The two whole-gap sweeps of that day asked every row of a wrong answer for a successful counterpart: the affine one left 10 of 30 answers running to the length limit, and the matched-context one took the recorded failure away, left 7 wrong answers whole and right, wrote 4 wrong answers a kinetic energy that is not their own, broke the line of the gain in 4 answers and moved each wrong answer onto its matched success's text. rule.reference: The original model (6a737131362433969a148503c92ef28cf7cf80648ac8ec74af19413a331b575c) and the compiled field (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/recipient-prefix-target-original/field, manifest 6451ca13d327218de140440b7f7cb2839a62e8b8890f49e275a11836d46b417c), both unchanged throughout; the cohort controlled-bf16-1's 30 fitting answers (15 wrong, 15 correct).
rule.objective: Astra's, as `objective` states it. Nothing of the field is subtracted, shrunk, thresholded, cropped or weighed again.
rule.proposal: One sweep (pipeline.weight_edit.gap_run), each of the 70 matrices once, in path order. For each matrix: one recorder pass of the working file as it then stands gives the matrix's rows on the recordings' text, every answer step and question position of the 30 answers; every row is asked its own request at the matrix's own merge and, for a feed-forward, at its layer's last merge as well (the model's last merge read as the output norm passes it on); the matrix is solved as one least squares over all rows with each output coordinate counted by the block's learned scale (pipeline/weight_edit/field.py); its ridges are the least squares' own unit times powers of two, from a ridge that moves no weight of the file down to the decomposition's numerical resolution; three paths, each with one of the case families' three groups left out, are read on the group left out; the rule `least held` takes the power at which the three groups left out together are left least (the larger ridge on a tie) and leaves the matrix as it stands where no power reads under it; at that power the matrix is solved on all 30 answers and written into the working file's BF16 weight by weight. Then the next matrix, on the file as it now is.
rule.what_is_not_done: No second sweep, no stage or dose loop, no ridge family beside the one above, no cap on a write, no chosen subset of matrices, no refit or rescale of a written matrix, no selection by an answer's token or sign, no second assignment of rows, no suffix dropped or given its erroneous original, no use of the no-fit answers or of reserved-40b, no choice between fields by their totals, and no continuation from this run's model without a new declaration with its reason.
rule.rows: The sweep's rows are on the supplied histories (the recordings' text, fed token by token); the swept model's own generated histories are read once, after the sweep. The two are named apart in every record of this run.
rule.held_readings: A matrix's readings on the groups left out construct its proposal and are kept in its record. They are conditional construction diagnostics on the recordings' text: every fitting answer has entered the matrices written before, and the field is made from all fifteen successes. They accept nothing.
rule.write: pipeline/weight_edit/gap_state.Working: one working file under <run>/sweep, each written matrix put where its binding lies with every other byte the original's; one record a matrix (the states before and after, every ridge's reading, the rule's ridge, what was written, how the rows were read, the solver's files as the process read them); swept.json binds the last state to the whole file's sha256.
rule.own_reading: Performance's readers under the reader protocol (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/whole-gap-recipient-prefix-original/reader-protocol/controlled-bf16-3.json), on card 0: own_text.py (the history check, the rollouts of the answers whose text changed, their registration on the original's computation), states_reading.py (the engine's own state at all 105 merges at every row of the model's own text), states_correspondence.py (whole-gap-correspondence/2), once for each of the two fields the one reading is laid on.
rule.comparison: The primary comparison is Astra's entry point (pipeline.weight_edit.whole_context_compare, records/retrospectives/2026-11-14-native-comparison-entrypoint-astra.md): the swept model's complete reading against the recipient-prefix field, beside the original's cached complete score under that field (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/recipient-prefix-target-original/original-score.json), every fitting member, every original reference frame and all 105 merges, each changed history through its recorded correspondence; per member and per group, with the changed histories listed. It reports and accepts nothing: no threshold and no acceptance value.
rule.fixed_reference: The same reading is then laid on the unchanged matched field (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/whole-context-targets-original/mates, manifest b09153baf5b6fe665b1cb990acccd7bddc7e5e131bb1a3491c2d765078c7cd20) by pipeline.weight_edit.fixed_reference_compare, beside the original's cached score under that field (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/whole-context-score-original/mates-score.json): Astra's arithmetic and checks called unchanged, a correspondence record and an output folder of its own, and no second capture, reading or protocol (fixed_reference_comparison). It is a separately labeled diagnostic of what changing the target changed. Its sums are not compared with the primary comparison's (two fields' totals are not one scale), it does not regrade the matched run, and it chooses nothing.
rule.readings_beside: After the comparisons this seat composes the run's result.json from its records, and reads the swept model's answers as the matched run's were read: what each answer states beside its question's own numbers, how far the answers moved onto one another's text, where an equals sign is written again, and the sweep's ridge readings (records/development/2026-11-14-whole-gap-solver: sweep_result.py, stated_numbers.py, text_pairs.py, ridge_grain.py, ridge_cost.py). Those programs name the two earlier runs; what they need to read this one is changed and committed before they are run on it, and named in the result. Where each answer's own text first leaves its recording is read against its sign row from own_text.py's records. A reading of the complete sums by kind of rows (question, before the sign, the sign and after) is not built; if it is, it is added by a dated revision that binds its program before it is run. Each is laid beside the matched run's record of the same name. None judges the candidate: the assessment is Astra's.

ridge_unit.derivation: field.Shared.unit: the trace of the least squares' own matrix over the input width. That matrix is the sum, over the rows solved on, of pull^2 x x', with x a row of the matrix's input as the engine multiplies it and pull the row's weight times how much of an output change reaches its state to first order (field.reaches; for a feed-forward the root of its two merges' squares). It is a sum over the rows and not a mean, so one power of two of it stands in the same proportion to the rows' sums on the two thirds of the rows a reading is solved on and on all the rows the written matrix is solved on. Computed for each matrix and each least squares from its own rows and recorded (`unit`); no value of another matrix is used.
ridge_unit.scales_with: The matrix's rows as the working file computes them, the rows' weights (the target's), the block's learned scale, the input width.

ridge_family.derivation: field.Shared.powers and field.path: the ridges are the unit times powers of two, from the power of the decomposition's largest value (ceil(log2(top/unit))) down to the power of its numerical resolution (floor(log2(resolved/unit)), with resolved = max(rows, input width) x float64's epsilon x top, under which a value of a symmetric decomposition in double precision is rounding), and upward from the first until a ridge moves no weight of the file's BF16, so every family begins at a matrix that is written as it stands. Both ends are the matrix's own; nothing is set. On the stand-in at all 70 matrices a group read 55 to 68 ridges, from powers 26 to 39 down to -27 to -30 (records/development/2026-11-14-whole-gap-solver/gap-map-counted/ridge-grid.json).
ridge_family.scales_with: The spectrum of the matrix's rows, the number of rows, the input width, and what the file's BF16 can hold of a change.

ridge_spacing.derivation: (Counted by ridge_grain.py from gap_map.py's 70 records, the stand-in's request with each matrix alone on the original's stored rows; ridge-grid.json beside it holds the readings one step to either side of each group's own least.) The step between two ridges is held to the grain at which the fitting answers themselves place a ridge. A ridge is taken by what three groups of those answers, each left out in turn, are left at (ridge_taken); each group also has a least ridge of its own, and how far those three stand apart is how finely these answers say where the ridge is. Counted at all 70 matrices on the family as it was read: the three groups' own least ridges stand 1 step of the family apart at the median (42 matrices; none at 13, two at 15), which with each group's unit counted in is 1.1 powers of two of the ridge itself (0.094 to 2.12). The value is two to that median count of steps: 2. A finer step would choose among ridges the groups place differently: one whole step beside the rule's ridge moves the three groups' summed reading by at most 0.016 of what the matrix as it stands leaves (0.0064 at the median), less than the three groups' own readings at that ridge stand apart (0.042 of what stands at the median) at 70 of the 70 matrices. What this does not reach: the count is of whole steps of the family it was read on and is no proof that 2 is the only step these readings allow. Of the ridges read, every second one (a factor of 4) would at its worst placement have left at most 0.0086 more and every fourth (a factor of 16) at most 0.027, more than the groups stand apart at 0 and 2 matrices: a coarser family is not shown to cost what the groups could tell. It is counted on the stand-in's request and not on a field a sweep is declared on; every group's every ridge is recorded for every matrix of a sweep, so the same count is read from a sweep's own records, where it is reported and changes nothing in the run. Nothing is claimed of a ridge between two of the family's: what such a ridge would leave is not read, the differences beside a least do not bound it (a reading that dips between two ridges shows nothing of the dip at either), no shape of the reading in the ridge is derived, and a matrix is written to the file's BF16, so the reading is not continuous in the ridge. No group's least is its family's first or last ridge (ridge-grid.json, 210 groups). The family lays out a declared, discrete set of proposals and is no size of a correction.
ridge_spacing.scales_with: How many fitting answers a group holds and how alike the groups are (the more alike, the finer a step they could tell apart), the request, and the matrix's spectrum; a finer grain costs proportionally more readings and no more decompositions.

ridge_taken.derivation: gap_sweep.least_held: of the powers every group's path read, the one at which what the groups left out are left at, summed over the groups, is least (the rows that ask and the rows that ask nothing in one sum); the larger ridge where two read the same; and no change of the matrix where no power reads under the matrix as it stands. The matrix is then written from all the fitting rows at that power of their own unit (field.written_at). A power is counted in each least squares' own unit: a matrix's three groups' units stand 1.06 to 1.08 apart, largest over least, on the stand-in (ridge-grid.json), so one power is one ridge in the three readings to 0.12 of a power of two. Accepted by Astra as proposal machinery: it proposes a matrix and judges no candidate. No number enters it.
ridge_taken.scales_with: The target's requests and the fitting answers' three groups (correction.case_folds).

coordinate_counts.derivation: field.Matrix.counts: each coordinate of a matrix's output is counted in the least squares by the square of the block's learned scale there over the scale's mean square (the scale is the file's own tensor, post_attention_norm or post_ffw_norm). An output change reaches the state through that scale, and a fit that counts every coordinate alike spends the matrix's change where the state hardly feels it: of the squared change the rows' goals ask, counted by the scale over counted alike, 0.069 at the median attention output and 0.13 at the median feed-forward (ignored/, 70 records).
coordinate_counts.scales_with: The model's learned scales, one vector a block.

norm_epsilon.derivation: The engine's RMS-norm epsilon, the model's own constant: a block's norm divides an output by the root of its mean square plus this. It is the engine's and is not set here. The solver's reconstruction of a merge with it is held to the engine's recorded states: on the original's stored rows the driver's reading of five merges against the affine compiled field is the compilation's own to between 7.3e-10 and 1.6e-08 of it (merges 25, 26, 48, 103, 104; real-fields/).

search_stop.derivation: field.unheld(width, error) = width x eps32^2 + 2 sqrt(width) eps32 sqrt(error): what a float32 state of that width cannot hold of a row's error where the row stands. A row's search for its goal stops when a pass gains it less. It follows from float32's epsilon, the state's width and the row's own error; no number is set. What it costs is measured: on 1,030 wrong rows of blk.8.ffn_down.weight against the affine compiled field, 0.65% more of what was left than a search stopped at width x eps32^2 alone (0.0094% of what was asked), in 248 passes for 43,505; on requests a row can meet exactly the worst row ends at 0.0022 of what it asked behind a layer's merge (blk.8.ffn_down.weight) and at 0.036 through the output norm, 0.0025 at the median (reach/).
search_stop.scales_with: The state's width (1536 here) and each row's error; a model in another float format has its own epsilon.

step_shortening.derivation: (Algebra on field._on_the_sphere as it is written; no record is read for it.) A row's trial at part p of its aimed step is the ellipsoid's nearest point to where that part leads. The aimed step is minus the row's slope over twice its bend, so along the ellipsoid the row's error e falls at first: its slope in p at p = 0 is s = -2 x bend x |along|^2, with `along` the aimed step's part along the ellipsoid, below nothing wherever there is a step to try. A trial that does not lower the error shows e(p) >= e(0). The one parabola through e(0), that slope and e(p) has its least at -s p^2 / (2 (e(p) - e(0) - s p)), and because e(p) - e(0) >= 0 that is at most p / 2: p / 2 exactly where the trial left the error as it was, and less the worse the trial. So 0.5 is the largest part a failed trial leaves standing whatever it failed by; the search takes it and uses nothing of the trial but that it failed, until a trial lowers the error or the part no longer moves the row's state in double precision (float64's epsilon times the state's size). At a matrix's own merge, after a pass that gained, the row stands elsewhere and its last failure says nothing certain of the new place: the part goes back by the same factor (2, the half undone), never past the whole aimed step, so a part is always the whole step over a power of two. Behind a last merge each pass begins from the secant's part (the last step's length squared over how much the slope changed along it) or from the whole bound's step where the last step showed no bend. What the factors can change is which trials a row's search makes, and so, within what the stop leaves (search_stop), where the row ends; no trial is taken that raises a row's error. What this does not reach: the parabola is a reading of three numbers and no bound on the error between them, and a part shorter than the half would also be allowed by it; what other factors would leave has not been read.
step_shortening.scales_with: Nothing of the data: the half is the parabola's bound for any error that falls at first from the row's place, and the doubling is its inverse.

written_format.derivation: field.written: a matrix is written weight by weight to the nearest value the file's BF16 holds, by the engine's own rounding (tube.bf16), and every reading is of the matrix as written. A change under half a step of a weight is lost; each ridge's record says how many weights moved and how large the written change is beside the asked one.
written_format.scales_with: The file's format and each weight's size.

memory_blocks.derivation: (The model's own tensor shapes, and the solver's text, code/signal-trace/pipeline/weight_edit/field.py.) field.BLOCK, the rows multiplied or summed at once, is the narrowest input among the matrices a sweep solves. Of the model's 70 attention-output and feed-forward-down matrices, 28 take an input 2,048 wide, 7 take an input 4,096 wide, 15 take an input 6,144 wide, 20 take an input 12,288 wide: the narrowest is 2,048. With that number no block of rows (BLOCK x input width) is larger at any matrix than the sums it is added into (input width x input width), and no larger number has that at every matrix. A sweep holds the number to its own matrices and refuses to start where their narrowest input is another (gap_run.block_held; a test holds the refusal). One block of the widest input, 12,288 wide, is 0.19 GiB in double precision. The solver's second size (the rows whose last merge's stretch is found at once, 256 until commit 24607439) is no number of the solver's now: field.Final.stretch reads as many rows at once as the per-layer gate's output is wide (gate.shape[1]: 256 in every layer of this model, the width of the matrices it decomposes there), which is the number it held. Neither puts a row into a sum or takes one out, and neither changes what a row's bound is computed from. BLOCK does cut the sums: a sum made block by block adds its rows in another order than one made at once, so another size can change a sum in its last digits, as another card does (records/development/2026-11-10-speed-review/README.md, "What is left of a solve": the two cards do not give the same sums). The number stood at 2,048 before this rule was written, taken as a size that kept the work inside a 16 GB card; the rule gives the same number for this model, so no sum of an earlier record is another. A matrix's record names the solver's file it ran, which holds the number.
memory_blocks.scales_with: The narrowest input among the matrices swept, which is the model's; for the stretch, the per-layer gate's output width. The order of a sum's additions follows the first.

ends_of_the_one_dimensional_search.derivation: Replaced: the solver holds no number here now (code/signal-trace/pipeline/weight_edit/field.py, field.nearest). Until commit 24607439 field.nearest ended Newton's steps when a step was under 4 of float64's epsilon times the unknown and began its bracket 32 of them wide, two small multiples no record derived. Now Newton's steps are taken until a step no longer raises the double that holds the unknown; the two ends begin one last place of that double to either side and are moved out, twice as far each time, until the length says they hold the root; and the bisection ends when a double holds no point between the two ends. That is one binary search, outward and then inward, in the double's own places: its doubling and its halving are the bisection's, and it has no number of its own. Where the search ends is what it was: the length never rises with the unknown as it is computed, so there is one pair of neighbouring doubles at which the output stops being longer than the radius, and the search ends on it wherever it began (tests.test_field holds the output to the bisection's alone bit for bit at every size of step, and a row nothing pulls at its least-scaled coordinate is left to the bisection). On the model's own rows: feed-forward 8's 19,751 rows against the affine field (real_fields.py, every row's goal sought at its own merge and behind its layer's last merge) give with this search the record the search before gave, every field of it but the seconds: 253 passes, the same largest step left and the same sums of what the matrix as it stands leaves. What this does not reach: records/development/2026-11-10-speed-review/solve-arithmetic/nearest_by_newton.py read the earlier form at four sizes of step and was not run again on this one; how many readings of the length the search now makes is not counted; and one matrix's rows are one matrix's.

matrices_swept.derivation: Every attention-output and feed-forward-down matrix of the model's 35 layers, in path order (gap_run.path_order: each layer's attention output, then its feed-forward down, first layer to last), each visited once. None is chosen and none is left out: the method's step 5 sweeps the whole path, and the number of matrices is an outcome only in how many the rule writes.

groups_left_out.derivation: correction.case_folds on tube.picks' three groups of the 30 fitting answers (15 wrong, 15 correct): the case families' folds, as in every solve since November 12, so that an answer and its family's other answers are left out together. Each is left out in turn to read a ridge (ridge_taken); the matrix is then written from all 30. They are construction data and no test (Astra, records/retrospectives/2026-11-14-whole-gap-native-rule-astra.md).
groups_left_out.scales_with: The cohort's case families and how many answers each holds.

late_start.value: observe-stream-late, only for kinds of step this sweep has compared whole across a real write
late_start.derivation: Astra's admission (774a4c04) and Performance's installation (2e7a7707, 273eb8d3): a pass may be started late from the two outputs the pass before recorded. In this sweep it supplies rows only for a kind of step (pipeline/acquisition/late_start.kinds) that the sweep itself has first read both ways across a real write, the ordinary pass supplying the rows and the late pass compared with it whole, every answer (gap_late.Late.plan: 'both' until the kind has held, then 'late'); a kind that does not hold keeps the ordinary pass for the rest of the sweep, and each seed is handed over only while every matrix before it holds the same bytes and its own file the bytes its pass gave. No sampled-position schedule and no timing is promised from it; every matrix's record names the recorder and the seeds.
late_start.scales_with: The kinds of step of the path order and what the working file holds before each matrix.

solve_card.derivation: Astra's specification names the matched run's solve card and the canonical card-0 native readings under its lock. The matched sweep's solves were on card 0 (RTX 5080) (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/whole-gap-mates-original/declaration.json, parameters.solve_card), and the two cards do not give the same sums (3.8e-10 apart at the largest value of one matrix's decomposition; each repeats itself: records/KNOWN.md, "one matrix's sums made on card 0 and on card 1"). Every solve of this run is on that card, so that a difference between the two sweeps is not the card's. Nothing of what is asked depends on the card.
solve_card.scales_with: The cards of this machine and the card the sweep it is laid beside was solved on.

prediction: Stated before any command of this run. (1) The construction, on the recordings' text (a conditional diagnostic and no acceptance): the rule writes a change at more than half of the 70 matrices (the matched sweep: all 70), and the writes are smaller at the median than the matched sweep's 0.057 of a matrix, since 4,907 more rows ask to stay; they are not predicted to fall under 1% of a matrix. (2) The primary comparison, on the swept model's own answers on card 0: (a) the 15 wrong members' sum against the field falls below the original's 0.058182 (all of the control's 0.058182 but the correct members' 1.04e-14); (b) the correct members' sum rises by less than the wrong members' falls, so the complete sum is strictly below the control's; (c) the correct members' sum stands below the 0.036329 the matched sweep left them at, which is comparable because a correct answer's targets are the same in both fields: if what moved the correct answers was the request that rows much like theirs take another question's state, it falls with that request gone. Known beforehand against (b): in both earlier sweeps the correct members' rise was larger than the wrong members' fall, and this run keeps the rule that wrote them. (3) The answers, a diagnostic beside the trace and never its judge: (a) no wrong answer writes a kinetic energy that is not its own (the matched sweep: 4); (b) fewer answers write the gain twice or an equals sign again (the matched sweep: 4 answers, and 14 places in 8 answers); (c) a wrong answer shares fewer of its lines with a success its target was made of than after the matched sweep (0.65 at the median; 0.27 in the original's answers); (d) no wrong answer states the gain subtracted, more than the matched sweep's 7 wrong answers come out whole and right, and the correct ones keep theirs (the matched sweep: 14 of 15). Not predicted: that the text before the sign stays the recording's token for token (repeating_pattern_check, 5), by how much any sum moves, which layers carry it, or that a lower sum is a repair. The fixed-reference diagnostic is predicted in nothing: it is read.
would_weaken_it: Astra's four, in what this run measures, and one of this seat's. WP1, the copying persists: a wrong answer again writes a kinetic energy that is not its own, or the wrong answers share as many of their lines with their matched successes as after the matched sweep. The request before the sign was then not what made the model copy. WP2, the correction is lost: wrong answers state the gain subtracted again, or the wrong members' sum does not fall below the control's, or fewer wrong answers than the matched sweep's come out whole and right. Keeping the rows before the sign then removed what was useful, and the gap does not begin at the sign. WP3, a number that is not the question's or a broken formula stands from the sign on: an available energy that reads as the gain twice or as another sum, or an equals sign written again on a line after the sign's. The counterpart asked from the sign on then carries the same defect the one before it did. WP4, the matrices' held readings fall again and the complete sum on the model's own answers does not. Local gains then do not add up along the path or do not survive the model's own text, whatever the rows before the sign are asked. WP5, this seat's: the correct members' sum is not below the matched sweep's. What moves the correct answers is then not the request before the sign but the request from the sign on or the size of the rule's writes, and the next question is the rule's, not the field's. Against the round's hypothesis itself this run speaks weakly either way: the field is a construction from fifteen successes and one recorded row an answer. An unfavorable result is kept and reported as it is.
limits: The field is an experimental objective and no validated capability target: a lower sum under it is not a repair. The primary comparison's sums and the fixed-reference diagnostic's are under two fields and are not one scale.
The three groups left out choose every ridge and every fitting answer is in every write: the folds are construction data, not a test. No answer outside the fitting thirty is read.
The sweep's rows are on the recordings' text. The swept model's own text is read once, at the end.

One sweep is one draw. A solve does not repeat bit for bit and no repeat of the matched sweep exists, so the spread between two sweeps of one declaration is not measured: only a difference from the matched run that is large beside what the records show of a solve's spread is read as the field's (STATE.md, "A solve does not repeat bit for bit on a card").

The execution is not the matched sweep's in four things, none of which is asked of the correction: no other sweep runs beside this one; no command runs inside a memory scope; a pass reads its model file through as it starts (solver.since_the_matched_sweep); and the readers are bound by a later reader protocol than the matched run's controlled-bf16-1 (since controlled-bf16-3 the readers take their answers from cases.py and, with no selection given, read the fitting thirty as before: Performance, commit 0117c49d). The first whole capture and reading under the protocol this run names are this run's.

The rule is the matched sweep's although that sweep's own records show that a larger ridge, the largest within the three groups' standard error of the least, would have written 0.42 of the rule's size for 0.87 of its gain at the median matrix (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/whole-gap-mates-original/ridge-cost.json): no run has used such a rule, and changing it here would vary two things at once.
The 4 wrong answers whose mass and speed no fitting success has keep, from the sign on, a counterpart made of questions with other numbers.

A row that asks to stay asks for the original's state on the recording's text. Where that state already holds part of the defect the field asks to keep it, and on the text the swept model writes the request is read through the recorded correspondence, which is complete and monotonic and no proof that paired rows are the same reasoning.

The search behind the model's last merge steps in the state's own metric and not the output norm's (records/development/2026-11-14-whole-gap-solver/README.md, "The search behind a layer's last merge, on the model's rows"), and the factor of two between ridges is held to a count made on a stand-in's request (parameters.ridge_spacing): both as in the matched sweep.
A defect the run finds in the driver or in the second comparison's program is fixed by a dated revision of this declaration that names the files changed.

revisions.authority: Marcos's decision of the evening of November 14, 2026, relayed to the three seats by the claude-research session as his (received there at 8:48 PM CT and relayed at 8:49 PM CT, by that session's own correction of its first time) and passed on by weight-research-astra, the objective's owner, as a stop of this run and the withdrawal of its execution admission (journal/2026-11-14-iterative-gap-closure.md, which states what was understood and is no wording to match): everything running stops, this run included, and the strategy is revised before anything else is declared.
revisions.what: The sweep is stopped at 10 of 70 matrices and is not started again. Its command (run.sh sweep, in this seat's session, 8:39:02 PM CT to 8:53:32 PM CT) was ended by this seat's interrupt signal to the driver's process, sent as the late pass of the next matrix (blk.5.attn_output.weight) had just begun (8:53:31 PM CT), the last write having ended at 8:53:26 PM CT, so that no write to the working file was in flight; the pass's recorder ended with the driver and the command exited with 130. No own text, reading, correspondence or comparison of this run was made, and none is made.
revisions.why: One sweep of the whole path is one step of a correction, and this seat's runs treated it as an experiment with a verdict: the matched sweep left the wrong members' sum under its field at 0.049883 where the original's is 0.067494 and was then read by its answers, and this run started again from the original against another field, which cannot tell a target that is wrong from a correction that is unfinished. The direction is a loop that measures the whole gap again on the edited model's own computation after every pass, corrects what is left against the fixed original reference, and reads the answers only once the measured gap has closed; what the gap is measured as, what closed means and what a pass costs are being worked out by the three seats (journal/2026-11-14-iterative-gap-closure.md).
